newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains in sluggish market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains in sluggish market.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended easier in a market devoid of fresh factors on Monday.

Dealers said activity had slowed considerably ahead of the Japanese general election on October 20, though sentiment remained firm. especially on the shorter end of the yield curve, on expectations of continued low interest rates.
"The JGBs lost 50 points but that's done nothing to Euroyen futures," said a Japanese bank dealer.
"We're still looking at some more consolidation...We have to look at tomorrow's action to see whether this is going to be a correction," he added.
The lead March Euroyen contract ended at 99.31 against its IMM close at 99.32. June was more actively traded with a turnover of 7,630 lots against 5,020 for March. It ended at 99.15 against 99.19.
Dealers said June could soon become the front month as March looked like it had topped out near its contract high of 99.36.
December JGBs ended at 122.91 against their opening 123.40.
Eurodollar futures scarcely moved all day as a holiday in the United States and anticipation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), due on Wednesday, hampered interest.

"Technically, they still look quite bullish," said the dealer, adding that the market would scrutinise the CPI for confirmation the economy was not overheating following Friday's release of a relatively benign Producer Price Index.
December and March Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM settlements at 94.35 and 94.28 respectively. Volume for both months was less than 2,500 lots.
